transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Sara (Nexa): Sara here.
[00:07] Jorge (Nexa): Jorge on the call.
[00:09] Priya (Nexa): Priya present.
[00:11] Ethan (Redwood SE): Ethan here.
[00:13] Imran (Nexa): Imran joined.
[00:15] Maya: Cool, thanks. We'll keep this to 45 minutes. Main goals: check onboarding progress, access setup, and go over the small set of results you ran last week.
[00:22] Sara: Sounds good. Quick status: we created the test cluster and ran the initial inference jobs, but we hit some permission issues when trying to spin up the peering tunnel to your test subnet.
[00:30] Jorge: Yeah, I think the IAM role scoping was too tight — we blocked the cross-account route. I have a ticket open but wanted to confirm exactly which policies Redwood needs.
[00:40] Ethan: Ok, we typically need EC2/VPC describe, route table modify for peering, and a service-linked role for the agent. We can send a minimal policy.
[00:48] Priya: Also on KMS — we have a corporate requirement to use our vault for envelope keys. Is that supported? We couldn't get the private KMS flow to work in the test.
[00:57] Ethan: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. For the pilot we'll need the KMS key ARN and a grant so our runtime can decrypt. There may be some tweaks to IAM.
[01:07] Maya: I'll drop the SOC2 and a network diagram after the call. That should help Priya validate.
[01:12] Priya: Appreciate that.
[01:15] Sara: On the results — we sent a small batch of requests Monday. The average p95 latency looked around 420ms for 4k tokens which is higher than we expected. Wondering if that's the model or infra.
[01:24] Ethan: Can you confirm the model variant and batch settings you used? Sometimes auto-batching with small concurrent clients gives higher p95s.
[01:30] Sara: We used open-llm-v2-13b, default batch size, concurrency 4, no KV cache.
[01:36] Ethan: Ok, that helps. Two quick things — enable KV cache for repeated context and try lowering batch size or using continuous batching. Also check quantization profile; 8-bit may improve latency and cost but needs validation for quality.
[01:48] Jorge: Quick dumb question — continuous batching sounds like queuing; will that add latency for single requests?
[01:52] Ethan: Good question. Continuous batching aims to fill GPU batches for throughput but respects latency SLOs. For single-request low-latency cases we route to a low-latency pool. For your pilot we can configure a mixed pool: hot path low-latency and a high-throughput pool.
[02:06] Lisa (Nexa PM): Is that part of the Dedicated offering?
[02:09] Maya: Yes, Dedicated gives reserved capacity and you can split pools. For early pilot we can present a recommended config and show cost tradeoffs.
[02:18] Imran: For the test runs, do you have a standard benchmark script? Our team used a simple curl loop which might not be representative.
[02:23] Ethan: We can share the benchmark harness (rps, concurrent users, payload shapes). I'll attach it to the ticket.
[02:28] Sara: Perfect. 
[02:30] Priya: About encryption in transit — do you support mTLS for internal agent communication? We need that for compliance.
[02:36] Ethan: Yes, Redwood Private supports mTLS between agents and runtime; the control plane can be customer-managed. We'll include the exact cipher suites in the doc.
[02:45] Maya: On the open items: Jorge to deliver VPC peering details and an IAM test role; Priya to confirm KMS policies; Ethan to run a profiling pass on your sample request set and propose tuning; Maya will send SOC2 + network diagram and pricing.
[02:58] Jorge: I'll try to get the peering creds today but no promise — might be Monday.
[03:03] Maya: If you can't do today, Monday is fine; we'll plan the load test for next Tuesday then.
[03:09] Sara: For success criteria — we want p95 under 300ms for 2k token average and a cost target under $0.003 per inference. We'll share our evaluation doc by end of week.
[03:20] Maya: That's helpful; Sara, we'll use that to size the Dedicated suggestion.
[03:24] Ethan: Quick note on cost — quantization + batching can hit your cost target but could degrade some LLM quality on edge cases. We'll run A/B evals with your prompt set.
[03:35] Priya: Ok, what about logs and audit retention? We need 12 months of audit logs, SSO via SAML, and role-based access controls.
[03:43] Maya: Redwood supports SAML SSO and RBAC; audit logs can be exported to your SIEM or sent to an S3 bucket with retention policies. We'll include the export steps.
[03:52] Imran: Any gotchas for on-prem vs cloud? We're testing in AWS first, but might move to an on-prem hardened environment for prod.
[03:59] Ethan: On-prem packaging requires some extra ops: network ports, hardware requirements and HSM integration if you need it. For the pilot, cloud VPC peering is fastest.
[04:08] Lisa: Regarding timeline, how long to get a Dedicated pilot up once access is ready?
[04:12] Maya: Typically 2-3 weeks to provision and validate, assuming network access is provided. Load testing and tuning add another week. So about 4 weeks end-to-end.
[04:20] Sara: That aligns with our internal timeline.
[04:23] Maya: Ok, any other blockers we haven't covered?
[04:26] Priya: One last thing — do you store any customer prompts? We need clarity for privacy.
[04:30] Maya: By default, Redwood does not index or use customer prompts for training. We can sign a data-processing addendum and document retention policies.
[04:36] Sara: Good.
[04:38] Ethan: I'll follow up with an initial tuning doc: suggested batching, cache settings, and a recommended quantization profile to try.
[04:45] Maya: Great. Quick recap of next steps and action items — we should align on due dates.
[04:50] Jorge: Sounds good.
[04:52] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll send the docs and calendar invite for the load test. Meeting adjourned.
[04:56] (call ends)
